DIAGNOSIS READY: Metastatic Lymph Node Secondary to Colon Cancer.

The clinical picture of a painless, progressively enlarging neck mass in a 50-year-old male with a history of colon cancer is highly suggestive of metastatic disease, likely to cervical lymph nodes. Given your history, this finding requires further evaluation to confirm the extent of the metastasis and guide treatment options.
